title: A New Open AI Model, GLM-5, Aims to Replace 'Vibe Coding' With Real Engineering
summary: Z.

title: A New AI Model Generates Matching Video and Audio Together
summary: Lightricks released LTX-2, an open-source AI model that creates video and matching audio from a single prompt, plus tools to fine-tune it for specific styles.

title: An All-in-One Platform for AI Coding Agents Is Trending on GitHub
summary: Kilo Code bills itself as an all-in-one platform for building and running AI coding agents, bundling several tools developers currently juggle separately into one workflow.

title: A New Tool Turns Messy Documents Into Searchable Knowledge Maps
summary: Hyper-Extract is a free tool that uses AI to convert unstructured text, like contracts, reports, or research papers, into structured graphs and timelines with a single command.

title: The Team Behind Astro Is Building a 'Sandbox' Framework for AI Agents
summary: Flue, from the makers of the popular Astro web framework, is a new open-source framework for running AI agents inside sandboxes — isolated environments where an agent's actions can't affect the rest of your system.

title: GitHub Built an AI That Lets Any Employee Query Company Data in Plain English
summary: GitHub described how it built Qubot, an internal assistant that lets any employee ask questions about company data in plain English and get an answer back — instead of waiting on a data team to write the database query.

title: A Fully Open AI Model Pitches 'Sovereign AI' for Anyone Who Wants Control
summary: A new foundation model called Apertus has been released with fully open weights, aimed at "sovereign AI" — countries and organisations running capable models they own and control rather than renting access from a handful of US firms.

title: GitHub Copilot Switches to Pay-As-You-Go Pricing
summary: GitHub is moving Copilot, its widely used AI coding assistant, to usage-based billing: your activity now draws down "GitHub AI Credits" instead of a flat monthly fee.

title: A Free Dashboard Tries to Replace Doomscrolling With One Calm Screen
summary: WorldMonitor, a free open-source project, pulls global news, geopolitical events, and infrastructure status into a single real-time dashboard and uses AI to summarise and flag what actually matters.

title: An Open Tool Gives AI Assistants a Long-Term Memory
summary: Cognee is an open-source tool that gives AI assistants memory across sessions, so they remember earlier context instead of starting from scratch every conversation.

title: A Tool That Squeezes 60–95% of the Cost Out of AI Requests
summary: Headroom sits between your application and a large language model and compresses what gets sent in — tool outputs, logs, files, and retrieved document chunks — reporting 60 to 95 percent fewer tokens while keeping the same answers.

title: A Modern Rewrite of SQLite, the Database Hiding in Your Phone
summary: Turso is an in-process SQL database compatible with SQLite — it runs inside your app rather than as a separate server — but it's being rebuilt from scratch in Rust to add features SQLite has long lacked, such as better handling of simultaneous writes and built-in syncing.

title: A Small AI Model Punches Far Above Its Size
summary: Researchers released VibeThinker, an open model with just 3 billion parameters that, on reasoning benchmarks, reportedly matches or beats Anthropic's far larger Opus 4.

title: Valve's Steam Machine Goes on Sale
summary: Valve started selling the Steam Machine, a small living-room computer that plays PC games on your TV the way a console does.

title: Microsoft Locks In 20 Years of Power for a Texas Data Center
summary: Chevron signed a 20-year deal to supply electricity to a new Microsoft data center in West Texas.

title: An Open-Source Studio for AI Voices
summary: Voicebox is a free, open-source tool for cloning voices, dictating, and generating speech from text.

title: A Free Tool for Editing PDFs on Any Device
summary: Stirling-PDF, now the most popular PDF project on GitHub, lets you merge, split, sign, and convert PDFs in your browser without uploading them to someone else's server.

title: Running a 70-Billion-Parameter Model on a 4GB GPU
summary: AirLLM is a library that runs very large language models — up to 70 billion parameters — on a single graphics card with as little as 4GB of memory.

title: How GitHub Made Issues Feel Instant
summary: GitHub's engineering team rebuilt how its Issues pages load, using client-side caching, smart prefetching, and service workers so that moving between issues feels immediate instead of waiting on the network each time.

title: A Tech Leader Automated 40 Parts of Their Own Job
summary: A senior leader at GitHub wrote about how they now lean on roughly 40 small automations — built with AI and simple scripts — to handle routine parts of their day, from triaging messages to prepping reports and tracking follow-ups.

title: A Phone Keyboard That Types Without Sending Your Words Away
summary: FUTO released a new swipe-typing model for its privacy-focused phone keyboard, letting you glide a finger across letters to spell whole words.

title: A New Way to Drill for Clean Energy: Vaporise the Rock
summary: Quaise Energy says it drilled 100 meters into hard granite using beams of millimeter-wave energy that essentially vaporise rock, instead of a traditional grinding drill bit.

title: Meta Pauses an Employee-Tracking Program After a Leak
summary: Meta has paused an internal program that tracked employee activity after some of the collected data leaked inside the company.

title: GitHub Pushes Back on a California AI Transparency Law
summary: GitHub joined a coalition asking California to amend its new AI Transparency Act, arguing the current wording could unintentionally burden open-source software shared freely online.

title: ByteDance Open-Sources a Harness for Long-Running AI Agents
summary: ByteDance released deer-flow, an open-source framework for building AI agents that work on long, multi-step tasks — researching, coding, and creating content over minutes or hours rather than a single reply.

title: How Copilot Squeezes More Out of Every Token
summary: GitHub published a technical look at how Copilot decides what to feed the model and which model to use for a given request — trimming irrelevant context and routing simpler tasks to cheaper, faster models while reserving the heavyweight ones for genuinely hard problems.

title: OpenAI Unveils Its First Custom Chip, Built With Broadcom
summary: OpenAI revealed its first in-house AI chip, designed in partnership with Broadcom.

title: Google's Gemini Can Now Operate a Computer for You
summary: Google added a feature to its Gemini 3.

title: Cloudflare Makes a Common Login System Free for Everyone
summary: Cloudflare released self-managed OAuth — the technology behind 'Sign in with Google' style buttons — for all of its users at no cost.

title: Krea 2 Is a New Open Image Model Anyone Can Run
summary: Krea released Krea 2, a 12-billion-parameter image generator whose weights are open, meaning anyone can download and run it rather than paying for access through a single company's service.

title: A Cooling Design That Nearly Eliminates Data-Center Water Use
summary: Nvidia detailed a liquid-cooling approach for AI data centers that runs at a warmer 45°C, which lets the facility shed heat without the constant water evaporation that traditional cooling relies on.

title: Git Worktrees: One Repository, Several Branches at Once
summary: GitHub published a practical guide to git worktrees, a feature that has existed since 2015 but has become popular again.

title: GitHub Adds Limits to Cut Down Pull-Request Spam
summary: GitHub introduced pull-request limits that let maintainers cap how many open contributions a single person can have at once.

title: AI Reads an Entire Ancient Scroll Burned by Vesuvius
summary: Researchers say they have read a complete carbonized scroll from Herculaneum — buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD — for the first time, without physically opening it.

title: Apple Skips Its High-End M6 Chips to Focus on AI
summary: Apple reportedly plans to bypass top-tier M6 Mac chips and jump straight to a new AI-focused M7 line, split into Pro, Max, and Ultra tiers.

title: IBM Unveils Chip Technology Smaller Than a Nanometer
summary: IBM says it has demonstrated the world's first sub-1-nanometer chip technology, pushing past a size barrier the industry has been approaching for years.

title: Google Releases a 'DESIGN.md' Standard for AI Coding Agents
summary: Google Labs published design.

title: A Free Tool Turns Messy PDFs Into AI-Ready Text
summary: MinerU, an open-source project trending on GitHub, converts complicated documents like PDFs and Office files into clean, structured text that AI tools can actually work with.

title: GitHub Benchmarks Its Copilot 'Agentic Harness' Across 20+ Models
summary: GitHub published an evaluation of its Copilot agentic harness — the system that lets the AI plan and carry out multi-step coding tasks rather than just suggest a line at a time.

title: What Happened When 2,000 People Tried to Hack One AI Assistant
summary: A developer set up a public challenge inviting people to break their AI assistant — tricking it into ignoring its instructions or leaking information it shouldn't.
